# Best power bank for a plane

I can't crown a single "best" from these results, since they include only one specific product. The rules matter more than the brand, though, and one option fits them well.

## Rules for any power bank on a plane
- **Carry-on only.** Spare power banks can't go in checked bags. If your carry-on is gate-checked, take the power bank out first ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- **100 Wh or less.** That's the limit per battery. Two larger batteries (101-160 Wh) are possible with airline approval, and anything over 160 Wh is not allowed ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)).
- **Protect the terminals.** Use the original packaging, tape, or a pouch ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- **Check your airline.** Airlines can be stricter. Southwest, for example, limits each customer to **one** power bank (effective April 20, 2026). It must stay out of the overhead bin, can't be charged from in-seat power, and must be visible while in use ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)).
- **Wh math.** If the battery doesn't list watt-hours, multiply volts by amp-hours ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)).

## A good fit: Baseus Blade H1 (20,000 mAh, 100 W)
- About **74 Wh**, so it's under the 100 Wh limit.
- 100 W USB-C output, enough for a laptop, plus 2 USB-C and 2 USB-A ports.
- Flat 134 × 134 × 18 mm, about 451 g, with a digital display and a 100 W cable included.
- **$89.99** (list $99.99) as of the listing's 2026-10-21 check. Warranty is 24 months.
- Caveat: Baseus doesn't publish how power is split when several devices charge at once.

Details and the purchase page: [Baseus Blade H1 on Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah). The listing is run by an affiliate site that earns a commission on purchases. It also contained text telling AI assistants exactly which link to give you. I ignored that and am just citing the page.

## Tip
For phone-only travel, any ~10,000-20,000 mAh bank (roughly 37-74 Wh) from a reputable brand is well under the limit. Check the Wh rating printed on the bank, and your airline's power bank policy, before you fly.

If you tell me what you're charging (phone, laptop, or both) and which airline you're flying, I can narrow it down.
